originality.rationale: Compared mathematical implications rather than matching titles. The 2013 exact k-abelian factor-count framework determines endpoint compatibility but no minimal DFA for all adjacent-pair residues modulo a common m. The 2026 Rauzy-graph factor-frequency paper bounds distinct frequencies in infinite words and gives no such finite automaton or length-class limit. The 2026 WELLDOC result concerns modular letter Parikh prefixes of morphic infinite words. Related published-finding corpus modular scattered-subsequence records use subsequence counts, not adjacent edge flows. No searched source yields or implies the q*m^(q^2-q+1)+2 minimum or the 1/(q^2*m^(q^2-q)) density. An unindexed equivalent remains a residual publication-priority risk.
residual_risks: A specialist unindexed theorem about modular 2-abelian congruences or edge-count languages could already imply the same formulas.

value.rationale: All-pair local factor frequencies are a motivated second-order statistic of words (2-abelian / Rauzy-graph perspective). A sharp complete-DFA state cost qm^(q²-q+1)+2 for every alphabet and composite modulus quantifies nontrivial conservation savings from q² naive counters, while the period-m acceptance-density law reveals an exact arithmetic obstruction and long-input mixing. Neither is a one-parameter toy increment or mere reexpression of an existing table.
